name: The Saltwind Reach
tagline: A river-market frontier beneath the Great Ring.
intro:
Spring has come late to the Saltwind Reach. Above Brindlemarch the Great Ring hangs pale across the morning sky, as it has for every one of the four hundred and twelve years men have kept records here. Barges crowd the docks, the Guildhall bells count the hours of trade, and the price of bread has risen three times this month. No one at the Lantern can say why.

You arrive with little more than a name, a few marks, and whatever your past has taught you. What you make of Brindlemarch is your own affair.

settlements.name: Brindlemarch
settlements.description: A river-market town of timber and grey stone at the head of the Saltwind.

settlements.name: Kestrel Point
settlements.description: A wind-scoured fishing harbour where the Saltwind meets the sea.

locations.name: Market Square
locations.description: Stalls and handcarts crowd the cobbles beneath the Guildhall clock. Hawkers shout the price of salt and cloth; a crier reads the council's notices beside a weathered statue of the town's founder.

locations.name: The Gilded Lantern
locations.description: A low-beamed common room smelling of woodsmoke and barley ale. Travellers trade news by the hearth; rooms upstairs rent by the night.

locations.name: Saltwind Docks
locations.description: Barges and flat-bottomed riverboats jostle along the quays. Porters haul sacks of salt and grain; the riverboat to Kestrel Point leaves each morning.

locations.name: Guildhall of Weights
locations.description: Brass scales and ledgers fill the high hall of the merchants' guild. Here loans are written, licences granted and disputes over weight and measure settled.

locations.name: Ringwatch Archive
locations.description: A tower of crooked shelves built around an old brass orrery. Scholars copy manuscripts by lamplight; a reading desk can be had for a small fee.

locations.name: Hale's Forge
locations.description: Heat rolls out of the open forge. Tongs, hammers and half-finished blades hang from the rafters above a soot-black anvil.

locations.name: Temple of the Still Ring
locations.description: A round white chapel open to the sky, its floor inlaid with the Ring's silver arc. Healers tend the sick in the cloister garden.

locations.name: Town Hall
locations.description: The council's seat: a pillared hall with the town watch quartered behind it. Petitioners wait on benches beneath the mayor's portrait.

locations.name: The Narrows
locations.description: Crooked lanes behind the docks where the eaves nearly touch. Things change hands here that would not survive the Guildhall's scales.

locations.name: Ashby Mill & Granary
locations.description: A great waterwheel turns beside the millrace. Behind the mill stands a stone granary, its lower doors chained.

locations.name: Cobb's Fields
locations.description: Long furrows of young barley run down toward the river. A farmhouse with a sagging roof watches over the fields.

locations.name: Whisperwood
locations.description: Old beeches whisper in the wind that gives the forest its name. Mossy glades hide herbs that healers prize; deeper in, the paths grow faint.

locations.name: Sunken Observatory
locations.description: A dome of green-black stone half swallowed by the earth. Through cracks in its roof the Great Ring's light falls on corroded brass and fallen star-charts.

locations.name: Kestrel Harbour
locations.description: Fishing boats rock against a long stone mole. Gulls scream over the drying racks; the air tastes of salt and tar.

locations.name: Kestrel Fishmarket
locations.description: A covered market of slick flagstones where fishwives shout prices and foreign spice traders unpack their chests.

locations.name: The Tidewatch
locations.description: A sailors' tavern built from the timbers of wrecked ships. The landlord keeps a lamp burning in the window for boats still at sea.

item_types.name: A Primer of the Healing Arts
Ring-age astrolabe
item_types.description: A brass astrolabe engraved with the Ring's divisions, far finer than anything made today.

item_types.name: mill granary ledger
item_types.description: A tally of grain moved into the chained lower granary, signed with the mayor's mark.

factions.name: Guild of Weights
factions.description: Brindlemarch's merchants' guild. It writes loans, licenses trade and settles disputes over measure.

factions.name: Town Council
factions.description: The mayor and aldermen who govern Brindlemarch, tax its market and command the watch.

factions.name: Temple of the Still Ring
factions.description: Healers and keepers of the calendar who read the Ring's slow turning.

factions.name: The Narrows Crew
factions.description: Smugglers, fences and pickpockets who run the lanes behind the docks.

factions.name: Kestrel Fishers' Compact
factions.description: The boat-owners of Kestrel Point, who buy salt by the ton and answer to no inland council.

facts.subject: Corvin Ashby
facts.content: Corvin Ashby is mayor of Brindlemarch and owns the mill.

facts.subject: bread prices
facts.content: The price of bread and flour in Brindlemarch has been rising for weeks.

facts.subject: the mill granary
facts.content: Mayor Corvin Ashby is secretly storing grain and flour in the chained lower granary of the mill to drive up prices before winter.

facts.subject: the mill granary
facts.content: Some say the mill's lower granary is full while the market goes short.

facts.subject: Odile Varne
facts.content: Odile Varne owes the Guild of Weights a thousand marks, due by Harvestide; without a profitable venture or a partner she will be ruined.

facts.subject: salt trade
facts.content: Salt sells for roughly twice its Brindlemarch price at Kestrel Point, where the fishers need it to cure their catch.

facts.subject: spice trade
facts.content: Spices landed at Kestrel Point cost barely half what they fetch in Brindlemarch.

facts.subject: Jory Pell
facts.content: Jory Pell fences stolen goods out of the back of a cooper's shop in the Narrows.

facts.subject: Sabine Kroll
facts.content: Sabine Kroll means to undercut Odile Varne's salt and spice prices until Odile's creditors call in her debt.

facts.subject: the Sunken Observatory
facts.content: An observatory from the first years of the Ringed Age lies half-buried deep in the Whisperwood, west of Cobb's Fields.

facts.subject: silverleaf
facts.content: Silverleaf grows in the mossy glades of the Whisperwood; healers make salves from it.

facts.subject: Hedda Strom
facts.content: Captain Hedda Strom of the watch cannot be bribed and has long distrusted the mayor.

facts.subject: Corvin Ashby
facts.content: The mayor is said to be storing grain only to protect the town against a poor harvest.

premises.name: the old bakehouse on Oven Lane

business_templates.name: Bakery
business_templates.description: Turns flour into bread for the market.

business_templates.name: Brewhouse
business_templates.description: Brews grain into ale for the inns.

business_templates.name: Fish-curing works
business_templates.description: Cures fresh fish with salt for inland markets.

business_templates.name: Apothecary
business_templates.description: Prepares silverleaf salves. Needs a steady supply of herbs.

business_templates.name: Trading company
business_templates.description: Ships a chosen commodity between Brindlemarch and Kestrel Point to profit from the price difference.

npcs.name: Odile Varne
npcs.persona: A sharp-eyed woman in a salt-stained travelling coat. Speaks quickly, counts everything, never admits weakness, but is warmer to people who prove useful.

production.source: her saltpan lease on the flats

goals.text: Clear her debt to the Guild before Harvestide
Keep her customers from Sabine Kroll

requests.title: A salt run to Kestrel Point
requests.text: Odile needs 10 sacks of her salt delivered to Captain Isa Dunmore at Kestrel Harbour.

npcs.name: Sabine Kroll
npcs.persona: Elegant, smiling, generous with compliments and stingy with everything else. Always seems to know a little more than she says.

goals.text: Drive Odile Varne out of the salt trade

production.source: salt bought off the flats carters

npcs.name: Mirela Tosk
npcs.persona: Broad-shouldered and quick to laugh, with flour on her sleeves. Hears every rumour in town and repeats most of them.

goals.text: Keep the Lantern full and her cellar stocked despite rising flour prices

npcs.name: Brannoc Hale
npcs.persona: A slab of a man with burn-scarred forearms. Says little, means all of it, and judges people by whether they keep their word.

npcs.name: Ysolde Ferrin
npcs.persona: A thin, ink-stained scholar who peers over spectacles and loses the thread of conversations when an interesting idea passes by.

goals.text: Prove the Sunken Observatory is real

requests.title: The Sunken Observatory
requests.text: Ysolde will pay well for any instrument recovered from the lost observatory in the Whisperwood.

npcs.name: Brother Aldous
npcs.persona: A soft-spoken, grey-bearded healer who listens far more than he speaks and notices when people lie.

goals.text: Keep the temple stocked with silverleaf salve

requests.title: Silverleaf for the temple
requests.text: Brother Aldous needs 4 bundles of silverleaf from the Whisperwood glades.

npcs.name: Corvin Ashby
npcs.persona: A plump, silver-haired man with a politician's handshake and cold eyes. Talks endlessly about the town's welfare.

goals.text: Corner the grain market before winter

npcs.name: Tamsin Reed
npcs.persona: A floury, anxious man who sweats when the mayor's name comes up and keeps glancing at the granary doors.

goals.text: Keep the mayor happy and his own conscience quiet

npcs.name: Wenna Cobb
npcs.persona: A sun-browned widow with a voice like a gate hinge. Has no patience for townsfolk and plenty for anyone who will pick up a hoe.

goals.text: Get a fair price for her grain

npcs.name: Piet Lunder
npcs.persona: Weathered, short-tempered, and fond of shouting numbers. Keeps a tally-stick behind his ear.

goals.text: Keep the quays moving and the thieves off them

npcs.name: Jory Pell
npcs.persona: A wiry young man with a gap-toothed grin and too many pockets. Calls everyone 'friend' and means none of it.

goals.text: Turn a profit without catching the watch's eye

npcs.name: Hedda Strom
npcs.persona: A tall, grey-eyed veteran with a scarred jaw. Speaks in short sentences and asks the second question nobody wants to answer.

goals.text: Find proof of who fences stolen goods in the Narrows

requests.title: The fence in the Narrows
requests.text: Captain Strom wants a name: who is moving stolen goods through the Narrows?

npcs.name: Aurel Vance
npcs.role: guildmaster of the Guild of Weights
npcs.persona: An elderly, precise man in a velvet cap who weighs words like coins and expects contracts to be honoured to the letter.

goals.text: Keep the guild solvent and the market orderly

npcs.name: Isa Dunmore
npcs.persona: A salt-bitten captain with a booming laugh and rings on every finger. Respects anyone who has crossed open water.

goals.text: Buy enough salt to cure the season's catch

npcs.name: Old Fenwick
npcs.persona: A one-legged old sailor who tells the same three stories and remembers every ship that never came home.

goals.text: Have someone new to tell his stories to

secrets_at.text: Beneath a fallen star-chart you find a brass astrolabe, green with age but whole.

backgrounds.name: Dockhand
backgrounds.description: You've hauled cargo on rivers since you could walk. Strong back, few letters.

backgrounds.name: Guild clerk's apprentice
backgrounds.description: You learned figures and contracts in a counting-house until it went bankrupt.

backgrounds.name: Hedge herbalist
backgrounds.description: A village wise-woman taught you which roots heal and which kill.

backgrounds.name: Street orphan
backgrounds.description: You grew up in other people's alleys, quick hands and quicker feet.

backgrounds.name: Disgraced gentry
backgrounds.description: Your family name opens doors and closes others. You left home owing money.
